subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw grow first-class multi-index embedding memory, or keep current single-index memorySearch with narrower fallback recovery fixes only?
rationale: The requested design adds config, storage, migration, query-routing, ingestion, status, and provider-failover semantics that root AGENTS.md treats as compatibility-sensitive product/API direction rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Design multi-index memory
options.body: Sponsor a design/implementation plan for per-model indexes, canonical chunk state, active/fallback index routing, migration, and status surfaces.

options.title: Keep narrow fallback fixes
options.body: Keep this umbrella open only as context while resolving concrete single-index fallback bugs such as the separate fallback-latch issue.

options.title: Decline core scope
options.body: Close the core request if maintainers decide resilient multi-index embedding failover belongs in a separate memory plugin or external architecture.

recommendation.title: Design multi-index memory
recommendation.body: Sponsor a design/implementation plan for per-model indexes, canonical chunk state, active/fallback index routing, migration, and status surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The live issue timeline assigns this feature request to osolmaz, making them the best current human routing target for the product/API decision.
